body.rationale: The governing IPS is still a draft, so I weigh compliance as provisional. I favour candidates the CIO can build from with no hard breaches, plus covariance-aware methods that suit a late-cycle regime (§4.3). First, resampled_efficient_frontier: no hard breaches, effective N of 13.3, 4.33% tracking error, and a backtest Sharpe of 0.63. The resampling guards against estimation error in the return forecasts. Its reviewers' findings are about wording (the gamma direction, and Omega not carrying per-view confidence). Second, black_litterman: compliant, with a 0.70 backtest Sharpe, 6.1 effective N and the lowest tracking error at 3.01%. It shares the same gamma-labelling issue but is otherwise transparent. Third, max_sharpe: highest ex-ante Sharpe among the compliant portfolios at 0.46, but the 46% us_value position rests on a modest CMA spread and there is no shrinkage, so it ranks below the two methods that temper estimation error. Fourth, pc_researcher: the best ex-ante Sharpe (0.51) and a 0.70 backtest Sharpe with a moderate -10.9% drawdown. It breaches volatility and tracking error, and reviewers flagged that its Sharpe sits above the max_sharpe ceiling and that the stated IPS constraints were not applied. That keeps it fourth, as a candidate that needs repair. Fifth, tail_risk_parity: it is a covariance-based tail method in my own family but not my own proposal. It has 6.0 effective N, a -7.2% drawdown and a CRO score of 0.29, though it breaches the volatility, return and tracking-error limits. Its main risk is the near-zero cash semideviation in the denominator. My first choice beats my fifth because resampled_efficient_frontier meets every IPS limit and holds up in the backtest, with 24% drawdown against tail_risk_parity's volatility and return shortfalls that the CIO would have to repair. I flag hierarchical_risk_parity: it holds 91.9% in cash with 1.4 effective assets. The reviews call it a mandate failure, and its volatility is 0.65% against the 8-12% band. I did not flag the adversarial diversifier, because its orthogonality is useful in an ensemble.
